diagnostic_evidence.quote: we may observe that setting $(\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\alpha_3)=w_{V_{2t},e^{i\theta(s)}}$, $\alpha_3(s)\neq-1$ for all $s\in[0,1]$

issues.failure_explanation: The lift in eq:explicitweight3 divides by sqrt(1+alpha_3(r)), so it is well-defined only if alpha_3 never equals -1. Since alpha_1(s)=0 exactly at s=(2k+1)/(4t) for k in {0,...,2t-1}, alpha_3=-1 occurs iff sin(pi k/t + theta_1(0))=-1, i.e. iff theta_1(0) is congruent to -pi/2 - pi k/t (mod 2pi) for some k. The stated condition theta_1(0) != m pi - 2n pi/t neither excludes these values (e.g. theta_1 identically pi/2 with t=1 is permitted, but alpha_3(3/4)=-1 and the displayed curve blows up) nor is necessary (theta_1 identically 0 is excluded but safe). Hence the hypothesis does not ensure the displayed curve exists, and the proof's claim that alpha_3(s) != -1 under this condition is false.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the hypothesis by theta_1(0) not congruent to -pi/2 - pi k/t (mod 2pi) for all integers k, which is exactly the condition alpha_3(s) != -1 for all s; one-line correction with no loss.
issues.overall_effect: The d=3 clause of thm:weight: for theta_1 permitted by the stated condition the formula eq:explicitweight3 can fail to define a curve. The d=3 existence claim itself is unaffected (theta_1 identically 0 is safe and gives the equality case), but the stated hypothesis is wrong.
issues.title: thm:weight (d=3): wrong hypothesis on theta_1; permitted theta_1 make the displayed curve singular
issues.why_classification: A one-line correction of the hypothesis restores the d=3 clause completely; the method, conclusion, rate, and advertised scope all survive, so the defect is minor.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: to produce a weighted $(4t-1)$-design curve $\gamma_{(\alpha_3,\alpha_2,\alpha_1),\theta_2}$ on $S^3$ of length greater than or equal to $2\pi\sqrt{32t^4-8t^2+1}$

issues.failure_explanation: For t=1 with theta_1=theta_2=0 the stitched curve is gamma(s)=(1/sqrt(2))(1,e^{i psi(r(s))})e^{2 pi i s} with r=4s-floor(4s) and psi'=-4/sqrt(1-u^2); its length is the integral over [0,pi] of sqrt(32-8 pi sin theta + pi^2 sin^2 theta) d theta, about 14.3, whereas the claimed lower bound is 2 pi sqrt(32-8+1)=10 pi, about 31.4. Asymptotically the true length is about 4 sqrt(2) pi t^2, exactly half the claimed 2 pi sqrt(32 t^4-8 t^2+1) ~ 8 sqrt(2) pi t^2. So the constructed curve does not satisfy the claimed lower bound and the equality assertion is false. The existence claim for C >= 2 pi sqrt(32 t^4-8 t^2+1) survives because the true minimal length is smaller, but the advertised threshold is not achieved and the proof's length analysis is wrong.

failure_location.quote: for $d=3$ and $C\geq2\pi\sqrt{32t^4-8t^2+1}$ (with equality when $\theta_1$ is constant for some $\theta_2$)

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recompute the length of the stitched curve (for t=1, theta_1=theta_2=0 it is the integral above, about 14.3, not 10 pi; asymptotically about 4 sqrt(2) pi t^2) and correct or delete the false lower bound and equality assertion; the advertised existence range remains valid, only the sharpness claim is withdrawn.
issues.overall_effect: The d=3 clause of thm:weight: the displayed curve does not have the claimed length (about half the claimed bound), so the lower bound and the equality claim are false; the existence claim for C >= 2 pi sqrt(32t^4-8t^2+1) survives because the true minimal length is lower.
issues.title: thm:weight (d=3): false length lower bound 2 pi sqrt(32t^4-8t^2+1) and false equality claim for the explicit curve
issues.why_classification: A concrete displayed constant in a main theorem is wrong by a factor of about 2 and needs a genuine recomputation, withdrawing the sharpness claim, but the existence claim and advertised scope survive with a better constant, so the issue is moderate.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We then take $W_Y$ to be double the sum of all weights of edges of $\mathcal T_Y$

Defining 
\[D_t:=\sup_{y_1\in Y_t}\inf_{y_2\in Y_t\setminus\{y_1\}}d_{\Bbb{CP}^n}(y_1,y_2)\\]
for $d_{\Bbb{CP}^n}$ the metric on $\Bbb{CP}^n$ as in \eqref{eq:cpndist}, we have $D_t\asymp1/t$ as $t\to\infty$.

issues.failure_explanation: W_t is twice the sum of the |Y_t|-1 tree edge lengths. A longest minimal-spanning-tree edge can have length up to twice the covering radius rho_t (geodesic midpoint plus Kruskal argument), and this is sharp: for two points at distance L one has rho_t=L/2 and W_t=2L > (|Y_t|-1)rho_t/4=L/8. The claimed bound would force every tree edge to be at most rho_t/8, which is false; the valid estimate is W_t <= 4(|Y_t|-1)rho_t. Moreover the proof invokes pro:covrad for the covering radius rho_t asymptotic to 1/t, but pro:covrad concerns the maximal nearest-neighbor distance D_t, a different quantity; the covering radius bound rho_t ~ 1/t for designs requires a separate standard argument (with rho_t >~ 1/t following from |Y_t| ~ t^{2n} by a volume count). The conclusions W_t lesssim t^{2n-1}, epsilon_t ~ 1/t and length ~ t^{2n} survive with the correct estimates.

failure_location.quote: Noting from the definition of $W_t$ in Subsection \ref{sub:connecting} and considering the covering radius $\rho_t$ of $Y_t$, we can see that $W_t\leq (|Y_t|-1)\rho_t/4$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the estimate by W_t <= 4(|Y_t|-1)rho_t via the longest-MST-edge <= 2 rho_t observation, and justify rho_t ~ 1/t for complex projective t-design sets directly (standard covering-radius bound for designs plus the volume lower bound); the asymptotics are unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the paper's main approximate-design theorem contains a false intermediate estimate (off by a factor of 16 in the wrong direction) and a misapplied citation; the theorem's statement is unaffected.
issues.title: thm:main proof: false tree-length estimate W_t <= (|Y_t|-1)rho_t/4 and misapplication of pro:covrad to the covering radius
issues.why_classification: The theorem's conclusion is correct, but the proof's central estimate is false and its justification must be replaced by a contained nontrivial argument (a tree-length bound and the covering-radius theory of designs), so the issue is moderate.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the map $h:S^d\to[-1,1]$ taking $\omega\mapsto\omega_1$, whose preimages $h^{-1}(s)$ we equip with the standard spherical measure $\sigma$ normalized so that $\sigma(h^{-1}(s))=1$
$w_{X,M}$ constructed as in Section \ref{sec:weight} is a weighted $t$-design curve on $S^d$ of length greater than or equal to $\pi|X|$

issues.failure_explanation: The final equality (1/2) int_{-1}^1 int_{h^{-1}(s)} f d sigma ds = int_{S^d} f d sigma is false for d >= 3: the pushforward of the normalized spherical measure under h: omega -> omega_1 has density c_d (1-s^2)^{(d-2)/2} with c_d = Gamma((d+1)/2)/(sqrt(pi) Gamma(d/2)), which is uniform (1/2) only for d=2. Counterexample: f(omega)=omega_1^2 in P_2(S^d) gives (1/2) int_{-1}^1 s^2 ds = 1/3, but int_{S^d} omega_1^2 d sigma = 1/(d+1), which differs from 1/3 for every d >= 3. This holds for every choice of X, lambda, M, so w_{X,M} is never a weighted 2-design curve on S^d for d >= 3, and thm:weightconst is false as stated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must replace the uniform latitude weights 1/2 by weights matching the pushforward density c_d(1-s^2)^{(d-2)/2} of sigma under h (e.g. a Gauss-Jacobi quadrature rule with O(t) nodes, each carrying a weighted t-design curve on the corresponding fiber), which is new construction not present in the source; the stated equal-weight design-set construction cannot be repaired locally.
issues.overall_effect: The construction behind the weighted results fails for d >= 3 and t >= 2: for every weighted t-design set (X,lambda) on S^{d-1} and every M, the curve w_{X,M} on S^d satisfies int_0^1 omega_1^2 ds = 1/3 != 1/(d+1) = int_{S^d} omega_1^2 d sigma. Consequently thm:weight is unproven for d >= 4 (its d=2 and d=3 cases have independent arguments and survive), thm:weightstrength fails for t >= 2 and d >= 3, and the parenthetical claiming weighted 2- and 3-design curves on S^d of lengths pi d and 2 pi d, the figure caption fig:Weightex2, and the abstract's claim of weighted t-design curves of length ~ t^{d-1} on all spheres are unsupported.
issues.title: thm:weightconst is false for d >= 3, t >= 2: the uniform-latitude Fubini identity fails (pushforward density is not 1/2)
issues.why_classification: The central construction is false for d >= 3 with an explicit counterexample; the main weighted existence theorem for d >= 4 and the fixed-strength theorem for t >= 2 lose their only proof and advertised scope, and the source contains no repair, so the issue is serious.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: and a continuous, piecewise smooth, closed curve $\gamma:[0,1]\to S^d$

issues.failure_explanation: The identity int_L f ds = int_{gamma|_l} f + int_{L \ gamma(l)} f ds holds only if gamma is injective on l: the arc-length integral int_{gamma|_l} f counts points of gamma(l) with multiplicity (the number of preimages in l), while int_L counts them once. If gamma traces part of L twice, the identity fails and the stated error constant epsilon_gamma = epsilon + c(|L|+ell(gamma)-2 ell(gamma|_l)) is missing the multiplicity correction c(ell(gamma|_l)-|gamma(l)|). The lemma is applied in thm:const to the simple curve gamma_Y, so the in-paper applications are unaffected, but the proof as written is incomplete for the stated general hypothesis.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a hypothesis that gamma is simple (or injective on l), or correct epsilon_gamma to epsilon + c(|L| + ell(gamma) - ell(gamma|_l) - |gamma(l)|); routine.
issues.overall_effect: lem:overlap as stated for non-simple curves: the first identity in the proof is false when gamma traces part of L more than once, and the stated error constant omits the multiplicity term; the application in thm:const uses the simple curve gamma_Y, so no downstream result is affected.
issues.title: lem:overlap: the key identity requires gamma injective on l; multiplicity term missing for non-simple curves
issues.why_classification: Routine repair (add a simplicity hypothesis or a multiplicity term); the only in-paper application uses a simple curve, so no substantive claim is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
For any $\delta>0$, there exists a smooth $(\varepsilon+2\delta c,c)$-approximate 
$t$-design curve $\widetilde\gamma$ on $S^d$ of length $\ell(\widetilde\gamma)=\ell(\gamma)+\delta$.

issues.failure_explanation: As written, S is finite, so ell(gamma|_S)=0, not delta/2 (the intended object is an open set S tilde containing S with ell(gamma|_{S tilde})=delta/2, and 'S subset gamma(S)' should read S subset S tilde). Moreover, if ell(gamma~|_S)=ell(gamma|_S)=delta/2 then ell(gamma~)=ell(gamma), contradicting the lemma's stated ell(gamma~)=ell(gamma)+delta; the smoothing on S tilde must instead satisfy ell(gamma~|_{S tilde}) = delta/2 + delta, which makes the overlap error |L|+ell(gamma~)-2 ell(gamma~|_l) equal 2 delta as required. The intended argument is reconstructible, but the proof as written is inconsistent.

failure_location.quote: take $S$ to be the (finite) set of $s\in[0,1]$ such that $\gamma(s)$ is not smooth. Consider an open subset $\widetilde S\subset[0,1]$ such that $\ell(\gamma|_S)=\delta/2$ and $S\subset\gamma(S)$. We may then smooth $\gamma$ to any curve $\widetilde\gamma$ which coincides with $\gamma$ on $[0,1]\setminus S$ and satisfies $\ell(\widetilde\gamma|_{S})=\delta/2$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rewrite the smoothing step using an open set S tilde containing S with ell(gamma|_{S tilde})=delta/2 and a smoothed curve with ell(gamma~|_{S tilde})=delta/2+delta (chosen simple on the overlap); routine rewrite.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of lem:smooth is internally inconsistent (a finite set cannot have positive length, and the stated smoothing gives ell(gamma~)=ell(gamma), contradicting the lemma's ell(gamma~)=ell(gamma)+delta); the lemma's statement is standard and the downstream remarks (smooth versions of thm:const and thm:main) are plausible but unsupported as written.
issues.title: lem:smooth: garbled smoothing proof (finite set with positive length; length accounting contradicts the lemma's statement)
issues.why_classification: The statement is standard and the intended argument is a routine smoothing; the proof as written contains concrete inconsistencies fixable by a local rewrite, so minor.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
considering any $\delta_{d_{y,j}}\in[0,2\pi/N_Y-\widetilde\delta)$ for $\widetilde\delta:=\delta/(2(|Y|-1))$, we pick any $z_{y_0}\in y_0\subset S^3$ and iteratively define 
\[z_{d_{y,j}}:=g_{z_y}(1)e^{2\pi ij/n_y+\delta_{d_{y,j}}i}\in d_{y,j}\subset S^3\]

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed inequality only bounds the gap between consecutive descendant arcs measured from the same base point g_{z_y}(1). It does not control the arc of D_y at z_y (the attachment to the parent, at angle 2 pi j_0/n_{parent(y)} + delta_y relative to a different reference) against the child arcs, and it does not prevent overlap when some delta_{d_{y,j}} < delta tilde (e.g. delta_{d_{y,j}}=0 places the j-th arc at angle 2 pi j/n_y, which can fall inside the parent's arc). Hence the D_y need not be pairwise disjoint for arbitrary allowed choices, and then the count |union D_y| = 2(|Y|-1) delta tilde = delta fails. The defect is repaired by choosing all delta_{d_{y,j}} in [delta tilde, 2 pi/N_Y - delta tilde), a nonempty range since delta < M_Y implies delta tilde < pi/N_Y.

failure_location.quote:
We can observe that the sets 
\[D_y:=\{z_ye^{i\theta}\:|\:\theta\in[0,\widetilde\delta]\}\cup\{g_{z_y}(1)e^{i\theta}\:|\:\theta\in[0,\widetilde\delta]\}\subset\Pi^{-1}(Y)\]
are pairwise disjoint for all $y\in Y\setminus\{y_0\}$, as for any $y\in Y$ and $j\in\{1,...,n_y\}$, we have 
\[2\pi/n_y-\delta_{d_{y,j-1}}+\delta_{d_{y,j}}\geq2\pi/n_y-\delta_{d_{y,j-1}}>2\pi/N_Y-2\pi/N_Y+\widetilde\delta=\widetilde\delta.\]

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Choose the offsets in the nonempty range delta_{d_{y,j}} in [delta tilde, 2 pi/N_Y - delta tilde) and choose the parent attachment z_y to avoid the descendant arcs; one-line change, conclusion unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The disjointness needed for the length counts in lem:connecting, hence the exact constants in thm:const and the clean length in thm:main, is unsupported as written; the approximate-design conclusion is unaffected.
issues.title: lem:connecting: pairwise disjointness of the arcs D_y is not justified by the displayed inequality
issues.why_classification: The construction has the freedom to make a generic choice; adding the local restriction repairs the gap with no loss of any claim, so minor.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: A theorem \cite[Theorem 4.2(i)(iii)]{Ehler25} of Ehler states that the triple of the set $\{(0,0,-1)\}$, the curve $s\mapsto(2\sqrt{2}\cos s,2\sqrt{2}\sin s,1)/3$, and the balancing constant $1/4$ constitutes a hybrid 2-design

issues.failure_explanation: For f in P_t, the circle part of gamma contributes ((1-rho)/ell(gamma)) 2 pi avg_circle(f) = ((1-rho) 2 pi/(ell(gamma) s)) sum_{X_P} f, since the s-gon is a t-design on the circle. Expressing the hybrid 0-design identity as a hybrid t-design on (X union X_P, gamma_P, rho') requires the per-point coefficients to agree: rho/|X| = (1-rho) 2 pi/(ell(gamma) s) = rho'/(|X|+s) and (1-rho')/(ell(gamma)-2 pi) = (1-rho)/ell(gamma). These are consistent only under the condition rho ell(gamma) s = (1-rho) 2 pi |X|, and then rho' = rho + (1-rho) 2 pi/ell(gamma), not rho + 2 pi/ell(gamma). The remark's unconditional 'if and only if' with balancing rho + 2 pi/ell(gamma) is false: e.g. the Ehler example ({(0,0,-1)}, circle, 1/4) is a hybrid 2-design, but the formula gives rho' = 1/4 + 3 sqrt(2)/4 > 1, which is not a valid hybrid triple at all.

failure_location.quote: $(X,\gamma,\rho)$ is a hybrid $t$-design if and only if $(X\cup X_P,\gamma_P,\rho+2\pi/\ell(\gamma))$ is a hybrid $t$-design.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the correct criterion: the equivalence holds provided rho ell(gamma) s = (1-rho) 2 pi |X| (equal per-point weights for the set and the circle's s-gon), with new balancing constant rho + (1-rho) 2 pi/ell(gamma); contained correction of a standalone remark.
issues.overall_effect: The general upgrade criterion in rmk:hybrid is false as stated; the specific examples in the subsection (the Konig-inspired construction with balancing 1-1/|Y| and the simplex/cross-polytope triples) are verified directly in the text and are unaffected, but the remark's stated criterion and balancing constant are wrong.
issues.title: rmk:hybrid: false equivalence for upgrading hybrid 0-designs (wrong balancing constant; missing condition)
issues.why_classification: A self-contained false claim in a further-work remark with a clear corrected version (a condition plus a (1-rho) factor); no main result depends on it, so minor.
